Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who has traveled to Baghdad to attend the 52nd Session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), met and held talks with Fuad Hussein, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Iraq, on Sunday morning. The Iranian foreign minister expressed appreciation for Iraq’s hospitality and the excellent organization of the session, voicing hope that Iraq’s presidency of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers would be marked by success and valuable initiatives to strengthen the organization’s standing. Referring to the need for Islamic countries to pay due attention to issues facing the Muslim world, particularly the question of Palestine and the Israeli regime’s continued expansionism and warmongering in the region, Araghchi stressed the importance of strengthening dialogue and solidarity among Muslim nations to resolve differences, enhance cohesion, and promote Islamic unity in confronting threats. During the meeting, the two sides exchanged views on Iran-Iraq relations and bilateral cooperation in various fields, particularly economic, trade, and security matters. Araghchi also briefed his Iraqi counterpart on ongoing diplomatic developments related to regional peace and security, emphasizing that the Islamic Republic of Iran, just as it remains resolute and serious in defending its national interests and security, is equally steadfast in using diplomacy to prevent an escalation of tensions and resolve issues. The Iranian foreign minister stressed that the insecurity prevailing in the Strait of Hormuz and its economic consequences for countries in the region and around the world were the direct result of the US-Zionist military aggression against Iran. Nevertheless, he noted that the Islamic Republic of Iran had declared its readiness to restore security to the Strait of Hormuz, provided the United States ceased its acts of aggression and intervention, as proposed in Iran’s seven-point plan. The foreign ministers of Iran and Iraq also exchanged views on developments in the Arabian Peninsula and ways to help bring the conflicts to an end. Referring to the need to learn lessons from developments over the past decade, Araghchi stressed that the Yemen issue could not be resolved through the use of force and a blockade. Rather, it must be addressed within the framework of the UN Charter, with respect for Yemen’s national sovereignty and territorial integrity and the human rights of its people. He reaffirmed Iran’s readiness to provide any assistance that could help facilitate dialogue between the parties. Referring to the importance of ensuring that Islamic holy sites are respected by all, Araghchi emphasized that, given the firm rejection of the claim that Yemen’s army had attacked the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, repeating this false allegation would not serve the interests of the Muslim Ummah. He added that the claim should not become a basis for division and discord within the Organization of Islamic Cooperation.

item.title: Foreign Ministers of Iran Pakistan hold phone call
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who is in Baghdad to attend the 52nd Session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), held a phone conversation with Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Pakistan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, at noon on Sunday. During the phone call, the two sides reviewed a number of bilateral issues and the latest regional developments, and exchanged views on diplomatic efforts aimed at de-escalating tensions and establishing stability in West Asia.

item.title: Algerian Minister of State for Foreign Affairs meets Iranian Foreign Minister
item.description: As part of the Iranian foreign minister’s consultations with countries participating in the annual session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), Sofiane Chaib, Algeria’s Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, met and held talks with Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Iran’s Foreign Minister, on Saturday afternoon. The two sides exchanged views on Iran-Algeria bilateral relations and issues concerning the Muslim world, particularly Palestine and the expansionism of the Zionist regime. Referring to the continued occupation and genocide perpetrated by the Zionist regime in occupied Palestine, Araghchi described the Palestinian issue as the most important issue facing the Muslim world and humanity, stressing the need to strengthen Islamic unity and solidarity to end the Zionist regime’s impunity. The Iranian foreign minister also briefed the Algerian side on developments in West Asia and the United States’ interventionist and destabilizing actions in the Persian Gulf region.

item.title: Iranian and Lebanese Foreign Ministers meet in Baghdad
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Iran’s Foreign Minister, and Youssef Raggi, Lebanon’s Foreign Minister, met and held talks on Saturday afternoon on the sidelines of the 52nd session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) in Baghdad. The two sides exchanged views on Tehran-Beirut bilateral relations and ways to strengthen ties between the two countries. Referring to the Islamic Republic of Iran’s principled position on the need to preserve Lebanon’s territorial integrity and sovereignty, Araghchi emphasized Iran’s support for Lebanon in defending its sovereignty and national security against the aggression and expansionism of the Zionist regime.

item.title: Iranian Foreign Minister meets OIC Secretary-General
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Iran’s Foreign Minister, who has traveled to Iraq to attend the annual session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), met and held talks with Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed, the organization’s Secretary-General, on Saturday afternoon. The two sides exchanged views on issues concerning the Muslim world and matters on the OIC’s agenda. Congratulating the new OIC Secretary-General, the Iranian foreign minister stressed the importance of the organization playing an effective role in strengthening solidarity among Islamic countries and addressing common challenges and threats facing the Muslim world, particularly with regard to occupied Palestine. Referring to Iran’s status as one of the founding members of the OIC, Araghchi emphasized that the Islamic Republic of Iran expects the organization’s Secretariat to operate professionally and impartially in order to strengthen Islamic understanding and solidarity, and to prevent any suspicion of bias by the Secretariat for or against any member state. The two sides also discussed developments in the Arabian Peninsula and the escalation of conflicts. Araghchi underscored Iran’s readiness to facilitate dialogue and engagement between Saudi Arabia and Yemen. The OIC Secretary-General expressed appreciation for the Iranian foreign minister’s participation in the meeting and stated that the organization’s Secretariat looked forward to drawing on Iran’s experience and capabilities

item.title: Iranian Turkish Foreign Ministers meet in Baghdad
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who has traveled to Baghdad to attend the annual session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), met and held talks with Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on the sidelines of the session. During the meeting, the two sides discussed bilateral relations and the latest regional developments, particularly the situation in Palestine and the ongoing genocide of Palestinians. Referring to the theme of the session, “Dialogue and Solidarity,” the Iranian foreign minister stressed the need for Islamic countries to pay due attention to the Palestine issue and take practical measures to halt the Zionist regime’s crimes against Palestinians and help realize the Palestinian people’s right to self-determination. Emphasizing the importance of strengthening cooperation and coordination among Islamic countries, the two sides also discussed the need to make use of the capacities of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation to address challenges facing the Islamic world, including Islamophobia. The latest developments in the Persian Gulf region and the Strait of Hormuz were also reviewed during the meeting, and Araghchi briefed his Turkish counterpart on ongoing developments.

item.title: Libya’s Acting Foreign Minister meets with top Iranian diplomat in Baghdad
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who is in Baghdad to attend the 52nd Session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), met and held talks with Taher al-Baour, Libya’s Acting Foreign Minister, on the sidelines of the session on Saturday afternoon. During the meeting, the two sides reviewed Tehran-Tripoli bilateral relations and emphasized the importance of strengthening consultations with a view to further enhancing relations between the two countries. The Iranian foreign minister reiterated Iran’s principled position in support of Libya's national sovereignty and territorial integrity and unity, as well as the need to end any foreign interference in the country’s internal affairs. Araghchi stressed that security and stability in Libya are prerequisites for peace and stability in North Africa. The two sides also held consultations on regional developments and issues concerning the Islamic world. Referring to the continued occupation and genocide by the Israeli regime in Palestine, the Iranian foreign minister described the Palestine issue as the highest priority of the Muslim Ummah and the international community, and called for urgent and serious action by the Organization of Islamic Cooperation to end the genocide in Gaza and bring an end to the Israeli regime’s impunity.

Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who has traveled to Baghdad to attend the 52nd Session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), met and held talks with Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty on the sidelines of the session on Saturday morning. During the meeting, the two sides exchanged views on bilateral relations, regional and international developments. Referring to the rationale behind the establishment of the OIC, the Iranian foreign minister described the issue of Palestine as the most important issue in the Islamic world. Recalling the genocide of Palestinians and the crimes committed in occupied Palestine, he stressed the need for urgent and joint action by the Muslim Ummah to end occupation and genocide and bring an end to the Israeli regime’s impunity. Iran’s positions on regional developments were also discussed in the meeting. Araghchi noted that the insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz was a direct consequence of the aggressive actions of the United States and the Zionist regime, which began on February 28 and have continued in various forms ever since. Emphasizing Iran’s commitment to diplomacy and peace in the region, the Iranian foreign minister recalled that the Islamic Republic of Iran had consistently pursued diplomacy responsibly with a view to reducing tensions. However, he said, the American side had repeatedly reneged on its commitments and, most recently, violated its pledge just two weeks after signing an understanding to end the war. Araghchi also briefed his Egyptian counterpart on the latest diplomatic consultations conducted through mediators. Developments in the Arabian Peninsula were also discussed and views were exchanged. Expressing Iran’s readiness to provide any assistance to help end the hostilities between Saudi Arabia and Yemen, Araghchi stressed that 12 years of tensions and conflict had demonstrated that there was no military solution or approach to the Yemen issue.

item.title: Iranian Foreign Minister arrives in Baghdad
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi arrived in Baghdad to attend the meeting of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), where he was received by Iraq’s deputy foreign minister. Upon arrival at Baghdad International Airport, Araghchi paid tribute to the martyred Resistance commanders, Lieutenant General Qassem Soleimani and Abu Mahdi al-Muhandis, as well as their companions, at their memorial site.

item.title: Iran FM to Attend Annual Meeting of Foreign Ministers of Islamic Countries
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, departed for Baghdad, the capital of Iraq, at the head of a diplomatic delegation on Saturday morning to attend the meeting of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC). In addition to attending the meeting and explaining the positions of the Islamic Republic of Iran, the Iranian foreign minister will also hold bilateral meetings with a number of ministers participating in the gathering. The 52nd Session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers, themed “Dialogue and Solidarity as Two Essential Pillars for Advancing Peace and Sustainable Progress,” will be held in Baghdad on Saturday and Sunday.
